title: KVPath: Connecting Key-Value Representations Across Transformer Layers
summary: KVPath replaces the standard per-layer independent KV cache with a single full-dimensional base KV at the first layer plus compact low-dimensional delta KVs at subsequent layers (residual or rolling updates) to reconstruct layer-specific states. The cost is architectural: it requires training the model with this parameterization and custom cache-management kernels, so it cannot be retrofitted to existing pretrained checkpoints; the low-dimensional deltas also add reconstruction compute at inference. It can fail if the inter-layer correlation assumption weakens for some model families or scales, degrading quality, and the claimed gains are under matched parameter counts rather than on standard pretrained models, so real-world benefit depends on adoption by model providers.
rationale: The method requires training or fine-tuning a model with a new KV parameterization, which the reader's constrained infrastructure cannot support, so the practical path is to wait for pretrained models or kernels that integrate KVPath.

Reduces KV-cache storage by up to 68% for GQA (a 3.1x reduction factor) and 55% for MLA (a 2.2x factor) under matched parameter counts, while maintaining or improving model performance.
